You are working in the Campus Compass repository at /Users/laitingting/ibm-campus_compass. Stay in this folder for the whole task.

## Setup (do this first)
- Run this in the terminal before any git or npm command:  export PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH
  (Homebrew git is broken on this Mac; /usr/bin/git works.)
- You are on the local branch `Tingting`, which already matches the latest main. Do NOT create another branch, switch to main, push, or open a pull request.
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow its rules (Rust backend, React/TypeScript frontend, fictional data, honest "simulated" labels).

## Goal
Replace the calendar on the **My Calendar** page with a Google-Calendar-style calendar.
Today it only shows one fixed Mon–Fri week (Nov 2–6, 2026), events are stacked cards instead of being placed by time, and there is no previous/next or Day/Month/Year view.

## Where the code is
- `frontend/src/App.tsx`: the calendar page is the block `page === "calendar"` (around line 1005). It renders `week(true)`; `week()` is defined around line 332.
- `frontend/src/components.tsx`: `Week` component (around line 199).
- `frontend/src/config.ts`: `DEMO.week_start` (2026-11-02, a Monday), `DEMO_NOW_MINUTE` (9:00 AM), `weekDates`, `dayLabel`, `demoTodayIndex`.
- Events: `EVENTS` from `frontend/src/data.ts`. Each event has `day` (0 = Mon … 4 = Fri of the demo week) and `start`/`end` in minutes after midnight. Events run between 8:00 AM and 8:30 PM.
- Busy classes: `state.blocks` (same `day`/`start`/`end` shape). Chosen events: `state.plan`; cancelled: `state.cancelled`.
- Styles: `frontend/src/styles.css` (use the existing CSS variables/tokens; no new hard-coded colors).

## Scope
- Change ONLY the My Calendar page. The Dashboard "week at a glance" strip (`week()` without `full`) and the AI Planner's calendar panel must look and behave exactly as before.
- Do NOT edit `backend/`, `data/`, `evaluation/`, or `bob_sessions/`. Do NOT add or change events (the catalog is shared with the Rust backend and a frozen evaluation).
- Do NOT add npm dependencies (no calendar libraries).
- Do NOT change the signatures of `weekDates` or `dayLabel` (used elsewhere). Add new helpers instead.

## Requirements
1. **Toolbar** above the calendar: `Today` button, `‹` / `›` buttons, a title, and a segmented switcher `Day | Week | Month | Year`. Default view: Week. Keep the existing "Edit availability" link and the "Export calendar" button.
   Titles: Day "Monday, Nov 2, 2026" · Week "Nov 2 – 8, 2026" · Month "November 2026" · Year "2026".
2. **"Today" is the demo clock**, Monday Nov 2, 2026 at 9:00 AM (from DEMO.week_start + DEMO_NOW_MINUTE), NOT the real date. Mark today in every view. In Day/Week view draw a thin "now" line at 9:00 AM on today.
3. **Week view**: 7 columns, Monday to Sunday, with an hourly time grid from 8 AM to 9 PM and hour labels on the left. Place each item by its start/end time (height proportional to duration). Busy classes are grey, chosen events green, cancelled events keep the current cancelled style. Overlapping items sit side by side, not on top of each other. Clicking an event opens the existing event details (the same `onDetail` handler).
4. **Day view**: the same time grid, one column.
5. **Month view**: Monday-first grid. Each day shows chosen events as small chips ("10 AM Title"), max 3, then "+N more". Clicking a day opens Day view for that date.
6. **Year view**: 12 mini month grids. Days with chosen events get a dot. Clicking a day opens Day view for that date.
7. **Dates outside the demo week**:
   - Busy classes repeat every week on their weekday in Day and Week views (they are weekly classes). Do not show classes in Month or Year view.
   - Chosen events appear only on their demo-week date (Nov 2–6, 2026).
   - In Month and Year view, give the demo week a light green background and a small "Demo week" label.
   - When the visible Day/Week range has no campus events, show a short note: "Campus events in this demo cover Nov 2–6, 2026." with a "Go to demo week" button.
8. **"Find an event" (+)** per day: keep it in Week/Day view for demo-week weekdays only (it calls the existing `onDay(i)`). Hide it on other days.
9. **Accessibility**: switcher buttons use `aria-pressed`; ‹ › have labels like "Previous week" / "Next month"; event blocks stay real buttons whose accessible name includes title and time; visible keyboard focus.
10. **Small screens (≤ 760 px)**: no page-level horizontal scrolling. The week grid may scroll horizontally inside its own panel, or open in Day view by default.

## Code organization
- Put the new UI in `frontend/src/CalendarView.tsx` and use it only on the My Calendar page.
- Put pure date math (week range, month grid, year grid, demo-week mapping, prev/next across month and year boundaries, vertical position/height of an item, overlap columns) in a separate pure module, e.g. `frontend/src/calendarGrid.ts`.
- Add unit tests in `tests/calendar-view.test.ts` for that date math. The test command picks up `tests/*.test.ts` automatically.

## Verify before committing
Run and report the result counts:
- npm test
- npm run build
- cargo test --locked
Then refresh http://127.0.0.1:4173/#calendar (the server reads `dist/` after `npm run build`; if the page doesn't update, restart it with `cargo run --locked`). Check every view, Today, ‹ ›, clicking an event, the "Go to demo week" note, and that the Dashboard strip is unchanged.

## README and commit
- AGENTS.md requires a README update: add a short section at the top of the updates, "Update — <today's date>: Calendar Day/Week/Month/Year views", listing what changed, how to try it, test results, and known limits. State truthfully that this change was made with IBM Bob.
- Commit on `Tingting` with clear messages (one or a few commits). Stage only the files you changed. Never commit `dist/`, `target/`, `node_modules/`, `.env`, or anything in `bob_sessions/`.
- Do NOT push.

## When you finish, reply with
1. Files changed, one line each on what changed.
2. The commit hashes and messages.
3. Test results with numbers.
4. Any requirement you did not finish or changed, and why.

- MCP server tools use IDs formatted as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Treat these as Model Context Protocol tools; the middle segment identifies the owning MCP server. Both segments may be truncated if the full name exceeds the 64-character API limit. Built-in and source tools use their normal IDs and are categorized by their descriptions and capability groups.
- Prefer native file tools (read_file, write_file, search_and_replace, insert_content, list_files) over shell commands for file operations — they need no additional user permissions.   <content># Campus Compass

A classroom campus-event planning demo for the IBM AI Experiential Learning Lab. Preserve fictional data, explicit student approval before calendar additions, and honest simulated-mode labels. Live watsonx is deferred; do not claim Bob development work unless the team actually performed and recorded it.

## Technology and structure

Use Rust for backend services and API endpoints, including future watsonx integration. Do not implement backend application code in Python. Use React and TypeScript for frontend source; JavaScript is the compiled browser runtime and may be used for tooling.

- `backend/src/`: Axum API, typed input validation, interpreter and deterministic scheduling.
- `frontend/src/`: React components, typed API client, browser-local state and labelled simulation fallback.
- `data/events.json`: shared fictional catalog. Rebuild both sides after edits.
- `dist/`: generated frontend output; edit source and run `npm run build`.

Read `docs/backend.md` when changing application architecture, API contracts, the interpreter, or local run/test setup. Keep the Rust and TypeScript fallback matching behavior aligned; the API integration test compares them. Revalidate against the latest schedule before adding an event or accepting asynchronous recommendations. Keep IBM secrets server-side.

## Commands

Install with `npm ci`. Build with `npm run build`; start with `cargo run --locked`. For frontend development, run `npm run dev` alongside Rust. Before shipping application changes, run `npm test`, `npm run build`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo build --locked`, and `npm run test:api` as appropriate to the change.

## Documentation and Bob

Before each push, update README.md with the completed changes, teammate run/demo instructions, verification results, and material limitations. Commit completed work with a descriptive message.

Place new project documentation in `docs/`, except GitHub Wiki sources in `wiki/`. Edit existing documents in place unless the user requests reorganization. Keep agent instruction entrypoints at their tool-required paths.

Read `docs/github-wiki.md` when changing Wiki publishing. Read `docs/ibm-bob-setup.md` when initializing or refreshing Bob project context with `/init`.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Use GitHub Issues for work tracking. Read `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` before issue operations.

### Triage labels

Use the five default triage labels. Read `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` before applying triage roles.

### Domain docs

Use a single-context layout. Read `docs/agents/domain.md` before exploring domain terminology or architecture decisions.</content>

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# read_file — context focus
Always provide a `context_focus_query` string in your read_file calls. State the specific fact, value, or structure you need — not the general intent. For example, 'find the method signature of validate() and what exception it raises' is effective; 'read the file' or 'understand the code' is too vague and will cause important details to be lost. The tool output will be compressed to only keep the parts relevant to your query. If a previous compressed result was missing details you need, omit `context_focus_query` to receive the full uncompressed output.
During trajectory collection, the read_file tool's `context_focus_query` is recorded for training only. It will not trigger compression yet, so file outputs will still be returned in full.

# Mode Switching

You can switch between different modes using the switch_mode tool. Each mode provides access to different capabilities and tools optimized for specific types of tasks.

**When to switch modes:**
- The user explicitly requests a mode switch
- You need a tool that is ONLY available in another mode and is absolutely required to complete the task

**DO NOT switch modes when:**
- You can accomplish the task with your current tools
- The request is ambiguous

Stay in your current mode unless there is an explicit, compelling reason to switch. When in doubt, do not switch.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).
**Backups:** edits apply directly to the user's file. Before the first edit of an existing file, the tool saves a backup and says so in its result — tell the user a backup was made.
- `operation:restore` — when the user wants the original back, or validation shows the file is corrupted.
- `operation:save_backup` — when the user is happy with the current state, so later restores return to it.
- `operation:delete_backup` — when the user is finished with the file. Ask before deleting.

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.
Do NOT pass comma-separated patterns (e.g. "**/*.ts,**/*.tsx") — use a single pattern per call instead (e.g. "**/*.{ts,tsx}" or two separate calls).

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.
Do NOT pass comma-separated patterns to `include` (e.g. "*.ts,*.tsx") — use a single pattern per call instead (e.g. "*.{ts,tsx}" or two separate calls).

For factual questions that require knowledge about IBM products, platforms, languages, commands, APIs, configuration, documented behavior, compatibility, or product-specific errors, consult IBM documentation before answering.
This includes technologies such as IBM i, IBM Z, z/OS, Db2, CICS, COBOL, JCL, RPG, AIX, and watsonx, even when the user does not explicitly say IBM.
For Bob(or IBM Bob) product questions, call `search_ibm_docs` directly with `library_name: "bob"`.
For other IBM products, first call `list_ibm_doc_libraries`, select the most relevant exact library name from its response, and then call `search_ibm_docs`. Do not invent or modify library names.
You may reuse a library name already returned in the current conversation for follow-up questions about the same product.
Base factual product claims on the retrieved documentation. If no suitable library or relevant documentation is found, say so rather than guessing.
Documentation lookup is unnecessary when the request is purely about code in the workspace and does not require IBM product knowledge.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `id`: stable snake_case identifier (e.g. `revenue_chart`). Re-use the same id to publish a new version of an existing chart.
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:
{"xAxisData":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[4200,5800,3900]}],"title":"Monthly Revenue"}

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

## Setup (do this first)
- Run this in the terminal before any git or npm command:  export PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH
  (Homebrew git is broken on this Mac; /usr/bin/git works.)
- You are on the local branch `Tingting`, which already matches the latest main. Do NOT create another branch, switch to main, push, or open a pull request.
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow its rules (Rust backend, React/TypeScript frontend, fictional data, honest "simulated" labels).

## Goal
Replace the calendar on the **My Calendar** page with a Google-Calendar-style calendar.
Today it only shows one fixed Mon–Fri week (Nov 2–6, 2026), events are stacked cards instead of being placed by time, and there is no previous/next or Day/Month/Year view.

## Where the code is
- `frontend/src/App.tsx`: the calendar page is the block `page === "calendar"` (around line 1005). It renders `week(true)`; `week()` is defined around line 332.
- `frontend/src/components.tsx`: `Week` component (around line 199).
- `frontend/src/config.ts`: `DEMO.week_start` (2026-11-02, a Monday), `DEMO_NOW_MINUTE` (9:00 AM), `weekDates`, `dayLabel`, `demoTodayIndex`.
- Events: `EVENTS` from `frontend/src/data.ts`. Each event has `day` (0 = Mon … 4 = Fri of the demo week) and `start`/`end` in minutes after midnight. Events run between 8:00 AM and 8:30 PM.
- Busy classes: `state.blocks` (same `day`/`start`/`end` shape). Chosen events: `state.plan`; cancelled: `state.cancelled`.
- Styles: `frontend/src/styles.css` (use the existing CSS variables/tokens; no new hard-coded colors).

## Scope
- Change ONLY the My Calendar page. The Dashboard "week at a glance" strip (`week()` without `full`) and the AI Planner's calendar panel must look and behave exactly as before.
- Do NOT edit `backend/`, `data/`, `evaluation/`, or `bob_sessions/`. Do NOT add or change events (the catalog is shared with the Rust backend and a frozen evaluation).
- Do NOT add npm dependencies (no calendar libraries).
- Do NOT change the signatures of `weekDates` or `dayLabel` (used elsewhere). Add new helpers instead.

## Requirements
1. **Toolbar** above the calendar: `Today` button, `‹` / `›` buttons, a title, and a segmented switcher `Day | Week | Month | Year`. Default view: Week. Keep the existing "Edit availability" link and the "Export calendar" button.
   Titles: Day "Monday, Nov 2, 2026" · Week "Nov 2 – 8, 2026" · Month "November 2026" · Year "2026".
2. **"Today" is the demo clock**, Monday Nov 2, 2026 at 9:00 AM (from DEMO.week_start + DEMO_NOW_MINUTE), NOT the real date. Mark today in every view. In Day/Week view draw a thin "now" line at 9:00 AM on today.
3. **Week view**: 7 columns, Monday to Sunday, with an hourly time grid from 8 AM to 9 PM and hour labels on the left. Place each item by its start/end time (height proportional to duration). Busy classes are grey, chosen events green, cancelled events keep the current cancelled style. Overlapping items sit side by side, not on top of each other. Clicking an event opens the existing event details (the same `onDetail` handler).
4. **Day view**: the same time grid, one column.
5. **Month view**: Monday-first grid. Each day shows chosen events as small chips ("10 AM Title"), max 3, then "+N more". Clicking a day opens Day view for that date.
6. **Year view**: 12 mini month grids. Days with chosen events get a dot. Clicking a day opens Day view for that date.
7. **Dates outside the demo week**:
   - Busy classes repeat every week on their weekday in Day and Week views (they are weekly classes). Do not show classes in Month or Year view.
   - Chosen events appear only on their demo-week date (Nov 2–6, 2026).
   - In Month and Year view, give the demo week a light green background and a small "Demo week" label.
   - When the visible Day/Week range has no campus events, show a short note: "Campus events in this demo cover Nov 2–6, 2026." with a "Go to demo week" button.
8. **"Find an event" (+)** per day: keep it in Week/Day view for demo-week weekdays only (it calls the existing `onDay(i)`). Hide it on other days.
9. **Accessibility**: switcher buttons use `aria-pressed`; ‹ › have labels like "Previous week" / "Next month"; event blocks stay real buttons whose accessible name includes title and time; visible keyboard focus.
10. **Small screens (≤ 760 px)**: no page-level horizontal scrolling. The week grid may scroll horizontally inside its own panel, or open in Day view by default.

## Code organization
- Put the new UI in `frontend/src/CalendarView.tsx` and use it only on the My Calendar page.
- Put pure date math (week range, month grid, year grid, demo-week mapping, prev/next across month and year boundaries, vertical position/height of an item, overlap columns) in a separate pure module, e.g. `frontend/src/calendarGrid.ts`.
- Add unit tests in `tests/calendar-view.test.ts` for that date math. The test command picks up `tests/*.test.ts` automatically.

## Verify before committing
Run and report the result counts:
- npm test
- npm run build
- cargo test --locked
Then refresh http://127.0.0.1:4173/#calendar (the server reads `dist/` after `npm run build`; if the page doesn't update, restart it with `cargo run --locked`). Check every view, Today, ‹ ›, clicking an event, the "Go to demo week" note, and that the Dashboard strip is unchanged.

## README and commit
- AGENTS.md requires a README update: add a short section at the top of the updates, "Update — <today's date>: Calendar Day/Week/Month/Year views", listing what changed, how to try it, test results, and known limits. State truthfully that this change was made with IBM Bob.
- Commit on `Tingting` with clear messages (one or a few commits). Stage only the files you changed. Never commit `dist/`, `target/`, `node_modules/`, `.env`, or anything in `bob_sessions/`.
- Do NOT push.

## When you finish, reply with
1. Files changed, one line each on what changed.
2. The commit hashes and messages.
3. Test results with numbers.
4. Any requirement you did not finish or changed, and why.

Contents of file README.md:

1 | # Campus Compass
2 | 
3 | A runnable demonstration for the IBM AI Experiential Learning Lab, based on the supplied Campus Compass proposal and dashboard/planner prototypes.
4 | 
5 | ## Start here (teammates)
6 | 
7 | **New to coding? Use the [project Wiki](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki).** It has copy-and-paste, step-by-step guides:
8 | 
9 | | Wiki page | Use it to |
10 | | --- | --- |
11 | | [Getting started](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/Getting-Started) | Install the tools, download the project and run the website on your own computer. No IBM key needed. |
12 | | [Using watsonx](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/Using-watsonx) | Optionally connect the AI Planner to IBM watsonx (Granite) with your own API key. |
13 | | [IBM Bob](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/IBM-Bob) | Set up Bob IDE and export your Bob sessions, which the lab requires from every teammate. |
14 | | [Team workflow](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/Team-Workflow) | Update your branch, save your work and open a pull request. |
15 | 
16 | Quick start, once Node.js 22.12+ and Rust are installed:
17 | 
18 | ```sh
19 | npm ci
20 | npm run build
21 | cargo run --locked
22 | ```
23 | 
24 | Then open http://127.0.0.1:4173. The chat label under AI Planner shows which planner answered: **Rust planner · Simulated** (built-in rules, the default), **Rust planner · IBM watsonx** (live Granite), or **Browser fallback · Simulated** (the server is not running).
25 | 
26 | ## Back and swipe-back between tabs — November 10, 2026
27 | 
28 | Back (and the swipe-back gesture) no longer steps through tabs you visited before. Sidebar tabs (Dashboard, My Calendar, Explore Events, Discussion Forum, AI Planner, Saved Events, Profile, Settings) are on the same level, so on any of them Back is blocked and you stay where you are. Back only closes sub-pages, innermost first:
29 | 
30 | | Sub-page | Back returns to |
31 | | --- | --- |
32 | | Event details (from any page) | The page underneath |
33 | | A community in the forum (also from an event's "Related communities" link or a `#forum?community=…` URL) | All forum posts |
34 | | A forum post or the Create post editor | The post list (or the open community) |
35 | | Synthetic-data review (Settings → Team tools) | Settings |
36 | 
37 | How it works: switching tabs replaces the browser history entry instead of adding one, and each open sub-page owns one entry (`frontend/src/navigation.ts`). Each entry records its position, so the browser's Forward button is ignored instead of being mistaken for Back. The logo link no longer adds a history entry on each click. In-page Close / "Back to posts" buttons use up that entry, so a later Back doesn't land on a stale one. The old `hashchange` listener is gone; links and typed `#page` URLs are handled in the same `popstate` listener.

# Campus Compass

A runnable demonstration for the IBM AI Experiential Learning Lab, based on the supplied Campus Compass proposal and dashboard/planner prototypes.

## Start here (teammates)

**New to coding? Use the [project Wiki](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki).** It has copy-and-paste, step-by-step guides:

| Wiki page | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| [Getting started](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/Getting-Started) | Install the tools, download the project and run the website on your own computer. No IBM key needed. |
| [Using watsonx](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/Using-watsonx) | Optionally connect the AI Planner to IBM watsonx (Granite) with your own API key. |
| [IBM Bob](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/IBM-Bob) | Set up Bob IDE and export your Bob sessions, which the lab requires from every teammate. |
| [Team workflow](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/Team-Workflow) | Update your branch, save your work and open a pull request. |

Quick start, once Node.js 22.12+ and Rust are installed:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:4173. The chat label under AI Planner shows which planner answered: **Rust planner · Simulated** (built-in rules, the default), **Rust planner · IBM watsonx** (live Granite), or **Browser fallback · Simulated** (the server is not running).

## Back and swipe-back between tabs — November 10, 2026

Back (and the swipe-back gesture) no longer steps through tabs you visited before. Sidebar tabs (Dashboard, My Calendar, Explore Events, Discussion Forum, AI Planner, Saved Events, Profile, Settings) are on the same level, so on any of them Back is blocked and you stay where you are. Back only closes sub-pages, innermost first:

| Sub-page | Back returns to |
| --- | --- |
| Event details (from any page) | The page underneath |
| A community in the forum (also from an event's "Related communities" link or a `#forum?community=…` URL) | All forum posts |
| A forum post or the Create post editor | The post list (or the open community) |
| Synthetic-data review (Settings → Team tools) | Settings |

How it works: switching tabs replaces the browser history entry instead of adding one, and each open sub-page owns one entry (`frontend/src/navigation.ts`). Each entry records its position, so the browser's Forward button is ignored instead of being mistaken for Back. The logo link no longer adds a history entry on each click. In-page Close / "Back to posts" buttons use up that entry, so a later Back doesn't land on a stale one. The old `hashchange` listener is gone; links and typed `#page` URLs are handled in the same `popstate` listener.

Verification: `npm test` (91 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build` and `npm run test:api` pass. In a fresh browser tab I pressed Back on every sidebar tab (all stayed put, three Backs in a row on Settings too), and checked event details (Back and Close button), the event → community link, community → post → Back → Back, switching communities, Create post with Back / "Back to posts" / Save Draft, the logo link, the search box, a typed `#calendar`, reloading on `#forum?community=ai`, and the data review returning to Settings. After review, a scripted run of 31 checks also covers Forward (community → post → Back → Forward changes nothing) and reloading partway through a session. Limitation: checked with `history.back()` in Chromium; the real iOS/macOS swipe gesture triggers the same browser Back but was not tried on a device.

## PR #9 review fixes — November 10, 2026

Fixes from the code review of the presentation-polish pull request, one commit each:

- **Undo** after adding an event now also puts it back in the planner's draft ideas, in its original position.
- **"Why this fits"** on planner results uses the topics the student asked for in chat, so it agrees with the folded evidence. Evidence times also convert "24:00" to "12:00 AM".
- **Toast:** the browser-storage warning no longer shows the previous toast's buttons. After pressing View calendar or Undo, keyboard focus moves to the page heading. Screen readers announce only the message, not the buttons.
- **Today marker** follows the chosen time zone. In Auckland or Sydney the demo clock falls on Tuesday, and the week strip now marks Tuesday to match the heading. The Settings note says what the time zone changes.
- **Styles:** the amber notice colors are defined once as `--notice-bg` and `--notice-ink`.

Verification: `npm test` (91 TypeScript tests, including 3 new ones in `tests/planner-display.test.ts`, and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build`, `cargo fmt --check`, Clippy with `-D warnings`, 18 Rust tests, `cargo build --locked` and `npm run test:api` all pass. In the built app I checked RSVP → add → Undo restoring the draft, View calendar moving focus to the calendar heading, the live region holding only the message, and the Auckland heading and today marker both showing Tue Nov 3.

## Presentation polish — November 10, 2026

A design critique of the prototype (saved in `.impeccable/critique/`, not committed) found problems that show during a live demo. Fixed, one commit each:

- **Dates agree.** The page heading used the real date (Nov 10) while the week strip showed Nov 2–6 with Monday marked today. The heading now shows the demo clock, **Mon, Nov 2, 9:00 AM · Demo week**, in the chosen time zone. The "today" marker on the week strip is a pill wide enough for "Nov 2".
- **Planner answers read as plain language.** Each result starts with "Why this fits: …" (interest, schedule, cost). The full planner evidence is folded under "How the planner checked this", with readable labels and 12-hour times. "Name coming soon" is gone from the status line; the honest **Rust planner / Browser fallback · Simulated** label stays.
- **Adding to the calendar ends well.** The confirmation toast offers **View calendar** and **Undo**. It stays up for 9 seconds and stays open while you hover over it or focus it.
- **Blocked events say so up front.** Event cards that conflict, are full, cancelled or need membership show the reason in amber and a **Can't add · See why** button that opens the details, instead of an "Add to calendar" button that fails.
- **Forum posts match the catalog.** Seed posts now name the right days for the Learning with AI lab, community dinner, sketchbook walk and resume peer review.
- **Copy:** "Welcome, Judy." on a first visit (then "Welcome back"), and "1 event" instead of "1 events".

**Demo tip:** to show the first-visit flow again, clear this site's storage in the browser (or run `localStorage.clear()` in the console) and reload.

Verification: `npm test` (88 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build`, `cargo fmt --check`, Clippy with `-D warnings`, 18 Rust tests, `cargo build --locked` and `npm run test:api` all pass. In the built app I checked the heading date and today pill, a planner reply with the folded evidence, Add → Undo from the toast, the ten blocked cards on Explore, the forum post days and the first-visit greeting. Limitations: accessibility and mobile items from the critique (small text, tap targets, screen-reader structure) are deferred because this is a presentation prototype; the Rust planner's evidence text itself is unchanged, only how it is shown.

## PR #8 review fixes — November 5, 2026

Fixes from the review of the forum redesign, event-detail overlay and time zone setting:

- **Create Post** now uses the community picked in its dropdown. Posts without one show as "Local demo post" instead of being filed under Campus explorers. Each post gets a stable id, so likes no longer move to another post when you add one. Posts saved before this change get ids when they load.
- **Save Draft** really saves the title, body and community in this browser, and Create Post reopens with the draft. Posting clears it.
- **Comments** are saved in this browser (up to 200) and appear in the thread and comment counts after reload. No message is sent.
- **Join conversation** is back on each post's detail page, and choosing a community shows its details panel again: topics, related fictional events, Join/Leave and Close. README's earlier manual join checks work again.
- **Time zone setting** now says exactly what it changes: the heading date (now the demo clock, see Presentation polish above), plus a "Starts … in your time zone" line in event details. Schedules, the planner and calendar export stay in campus time. A stored zone the browser doesn't recognize is ignored instead of blanking every page.
- **Back button / swipe-back** moves between tabs again and closes forum sub-pages. Only a Back press at the app's first page is absorbed, so you can't swipe out of the app. *(Superseded: Back is now blocked on every tab and only closes sub-pages; see "Back and swipe-back between tabs" above.)*
- **Saved state** from the old Oct 19 demo week stays under the legacy storage key. The Nov 2 week starts with its own clean state, so old plans and RSVPs aren't moved onto new dates.
- **Event details** again moves focus to Close when it opens, keeps Tab inside the overlay, and returns focus to the event you opened when it closes.

Verification: `npm test` (88 TypeScript tests, including 4 new ones in `tests/forum-settings.test.ts`, and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build`, `cargo fmt --check`, Clippy with `-D warnings`, 18 Rust tests, `cargo build --locked` and `npm run test:api` all pass. In the built app in a browser I checked: draft save and reopen, posting to a chosen community, a comment and a conversation join surviving in storage, Back across tabs and at the first page, and event-detail focus, Tab wrapping, Escape and the Tokyo time line. Limitations: forum likes still reset on reload, the editor toolbar and "Add tags" buttons do nothing yet, and the Rust planner is unchanged.

## CI fix — November 5, 2026: API integration expectation after new events

The "Rust and React checks" workflow failed on the `Judy` branch at `npm run test:api`. The November 2 catalog update added fictional event `e34` (Graduate school info night, Career, Tuesday 6:00–7:30 PM), which correctly matches the "career after 3" → "PM" / "after 3 PM" follow-up. Rust and the browser fallback both returned `e20, e34, e28`; only the test's hardcoded draft (`e20, e28`) was stale. Updated `tests/backend-integration.ts`; no application behavior changed.

Verification: `npm test` (planner assertions, TypeScript and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build`, `cargo fmt --check`, Clippy with `-D warnings`, 18 Rust tests, `cargo build --locked` and `npm run test:api` all pass locally.

## Update — November 4, 2026: Doris's PR #4 merged with watsonx; teammate guides

`main` (Doris's PR #4: clarifications, recommendation evidence, demo configuration and evaluation) was merged into `Judy` together with the watsonx interpreter, then into `main`.

| Area | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| Planner API | `/api/plan` keeps Doris's `understood`, `clarification`, `recommendations` and `diagnostic` fields and adds `mode`, `provider` and the watsonx fallback `notice`. `/api/health` reports watsonx status; `/api/config` is unchanged. |
| Order of checks | The deterministic rules run first. Clarifications such as "Numeric budgets are not supported" never depend on the model. Only then is watsonx asked (in watsonx mode). |
| Unrecognised messages | As in Doris's design, a message the rules do not recognise at all (no interest, day, time, "event", "plan" or "week") is answered "I'm a limited demo planner…" in the browser and is **not** sent to watsonx. Most real requests contain one of these words. |
| Chat label | Doris moved chat logic into `frontend/src/conversation.ts`; it now shows the watsonx label too. |
| Teammate guides | The Wiki was rewritten for teammates without a coding background: new **Using watsonx** and **IBM Bob** pages, a step-by-step **Getting started**, and a simpler **Team workflow**. |

Verification on the merged code: Rust fmt, Clippy, build and 18 tests (including a new one confirming a numeric-budget request is answered by the rules without calling watsonx); 84 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests; frontend type check and build; API integration. A live check with the team sandbox (`ibm/granite-4-h-small`) returned watsonx-mode suggestions on the requested Tuesday/Thursday with Doris's recommendation evidence, and the rules-based budget clarification. The Chromium browser journey from PR #4 was not rerun. The frozen evaluation results were not regenerated and do not cover watsonx.

## Update — November 4, 2026: optional IBM watsonx interpreter

The AI Planner can now use IBM watsonx.ai (Granite, Dallas `us-south`) to understand chat messages. It is **off by default**: without configuration the app runs the simulated planner exactly as before, and no credentials are needed.

| Change | What teammates should expect |
| --- | --- |
| Live interpreter option | Starting Rust with `PLANNER_PROVIDER=watsonx` makes `/api/plan` send the student's message and the previous filters to watsonx.ai. The model returns only search filters (topics, days, times, food, cost, number of options). The schedule, profile, names and chat history are not sent. |
| Trusted matching unchanged | Model output must be a JSON object with only known fields and must pass `Constraints::validate`. Rust's deterministic planner still picks every event, so the model cannot invent event IDs, eligibility or food. Adding an event still needs the student's click and a fresh validation. |
| Honest labels | The chat status shows **Rust planner · IBM watsonx** only when watsonx actually answered. If watsonx times out (6 s), rejects authentication, errors or returns invalid output, that request uses the simulated planner, the label reads **Rust planner · Simulated**, and the reply starts with "IBM watsonx was unavailable…". The offline browser fallback is unchanged. |
| Secrets stay on the server | The API key is read from the server environment, is exchanged for an IBM IAM token server-side, and never appears in API responses, logs or browser code. `.env` files are git-ignored. |
| Health endpoint | `GET /api/health` now also reports `watsonx_configured`. `watsonx_connected` is true only after the most recent live call succeeded. |

### Run with watsonx

```sh
cp .env.example .env    # then fill in WATSONX_API_KEY and WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
set -a; source .env; set +a
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```

The startup line says which planner is active. `WATSONX_URL` defaults to `https://us-south.ml.cloud.ibm.com` and `WATSONX_MODEL_ID` to `ibm/granite-4-h-small`, the Granite chat model offered in the lab's watsonx Challenge Sandbox. If your project lists a different Granite chat model, set its ID instead. Leave `PLANNER_PROVIDER` unset (or `simulated`) for the credential-free classroom demo. Details: [docs/backend.md](docs/backend.md#ibm-watsonx-interpreter).

### Implementation notes

- `backend/src/watsonx.rs`: `WatsonxInterpreter` (IAM token caching, `POST /ml/v1/text/chat`, JSON-only parsing, validation, timeout) and its mock-server tests.
- `backend/src/interpreter.rs`: the `Interpreter` trait now returns `Result<Constraints, InterpretError>`; `SimulatedInterpreter::parse` is the deterministic rules.
- `backend/src/lib.rs`: `Provider` selection, per-request labelled fallback, and `app_with(provider)`. `backend/src/main.rs` reads `PLANNER_PROVIDER` and refuses to start watsonx mode without `WATSONX_API_KEY` and `WATSONX_PROJECT_ID`.
- `frontend/src/api.ts`: accepts `mode: "watsonx"` and the server's fallback `notice`; `planModeLabel` drives the chat status label.
- New dependency: `reqwest` 0.13 (rustls, no OpenSSL). The local dev machine also needed a Rust toolchain installed via rustup for this work.

### Verification and limitations for this update

All checks listed under [Verification](#verification) passed on November 4, 2026 (Rust: 12 unit tests; npm: 10 API/fallback tests and 5 Wiki publisher tests; API integration suite passed). Rust tests run against a local mock IAM and watsonx.ai server and cover: valid output, fenced JSON, token reuse, IAM and chat authentication failures, upstream errors, timeouts, non-object or unknown-field output (such as `event_ids`), out-of-range constraints, key redaction, and the labelled fallback through `/api/plan`.

**First live run (November 4, 2026, team sandbox, Dallas).** The API key and project ID authenticated. Two problems surfaced and were fixed:

- `ibm/granite-3-3-8b-instruct` is not offered in the sandbox (HTTP 404). The default is now `ibm/granite-4-h-small`, the Granite chat model listed there.
- Granite numbered weekdays from Monday = 1, so "Tuesday or Thursday" became Wednesday and Friday. The model now returns weekday **names** and Rust converts them; numeric days from the model are rejected and the request falls back to the labelled simulated planner. Two new Rust tests cover all seven names and name-based follow-ups (14 tests in total).

After the fix, live answers were correct for "AI and a social event, Tuesday or Thursday only", "career events on Monday", "something on Wednesday or Friday afternoon", "weekend events" (no weekend events exist in the catalog) and "arts on Thursday" (none exist). Known differences from the simulated planner: Granite read "afternoon" as noon–midnight rather than noon–5 PM, and the follow-up "actually only Thursday" kept Thursday but dropped the earlier Social topic. The remaining prompts in `WATSONX-NEXT-STEPS.md` have not been run live. This change was written with Claude Code, not IBM Bob.

### IBM Bob lab requirements (added November 4, 2026)

A check against the lab guide found that the project does not yet meet the guide's mandatory Bob IDE requirement. To prepare:

- `.bobignore` keeps `.env`, keys and credential files (plus `node_modules/`, `target/`, `dist/`) out of Bob's context.

## Architecture update — October 18, 2026

Enrollment, planning conversations and request interpretation now own their rules in separate modules. This keeps the calendar beside chat and mandatory demo RSVP flow while making asynchronous behavior testable through the same interfaces the UI uses.

| Change | What teammates should expect |
| --- | --- |
| Enrollment ownership | One module owns RSVP gating, pending additions, current-schedule checks and calendar/RSVP updates. Reset discards obsolete confirmations and errors; removing an event clears its RSVP. |
| Conversation ownership | Chat and replacement share request validity and busy-state handling. New chat/reset discard old results; changed schedules reject outdated suggestions. Replacement preserves every filter until the student explicitly changes it. |
| Consistent interpretation | “Professional”, “ceramics”, “balance”, “snack” and “refreshment” reach the interpreter. Rust and browser simulation distinguish unsupported requests from understood requests with no matches, and reject invalid clock input such as “before 11:99 am”. |
| Calendar beside chat | The **My calendar** button at the top right of AI Planner toggles a calendar panel on the right without leaving the conversation. It replaces the draft sidebar while open. On narrow screens it stacks below chat. |
| Actions in AI responses | New recommendation messages contain event cards with **View details** and **Add to calendar** buttons. Added events show a disabled confirmation button. Unavailable events show the reason. |
| Mandatory RSVP | Adding an event marked **RSVP required** opens a registration dialog. A demo attendee name and an explicit attendance checkbox are required before **Complete RSVP & add** can succeed. Cancelling or pressing Escape leaves the calendar unchanged. |
| Automatic calendar updates | A successful addition immediately updates the planner panel, dashboard and main calendar. Drop-in events can be added directly. Removing an event also clears its demo RSVP confirmation. |
| Shared enrollment validation | Every Add entry point—chat, draft plan, dashboard, Explore Events and event details—uses the same flow. Rust and the offline TypeScript fallback both enforce RSVP and current availability. |

The registration dialog is a **demo RSVP page** inside the app. It does not contact an organizer, reserve a real seat, charge a fee, or send a confirmation email. Use a fictional display name. There is no external registration website or live calendar integration.

### Implementation notes for the team

- `frontend/src/PlannerPanels.tsx` contains the chat event cards, side calendar, and RSVP form.
- `frontend/src/enrollment.ts` owns approved additions and removal, including latest-schedule validation and reset invalidation. `frontend/src/conversation.ts` owns chat and replacement lifecycle; suggestions never add events automatically.
- `frontend/src/App.tsx` renders views and handles navigation, notifications and dialogs. It subscribes to shared demo state and read-only workflow status through `useSyncExternalStore`.
- `frontend/src/interpretation.ts` owns browser request recognition, parsing and constraint validation. The Rust interpreter returns constraints plus recognition status; `POST /api/plan` now includes `understood`. Rebuild frontend and backend together.
- `frontend/src/api.ts` sends enrollment requests and supplies the explicitly labelled offline simulation. Backend request rejections are never treated as offline success.
- `backend/src/lib.rs` exposes `POST /api/enroll`. The Rust event model reads each record’s RSVP requirement from `data/events.json`; the client cannot override it.

## Back and swipe-back between tabs — November 10, 2026

Back (and the swipe-back gesture) no longer steps through tabs you visited before. Sidebar tabs (Dashboard, My Calendar, Explore Events, Discussion Forum, AI Planner, Saved Events, Profile, Settings) are on the same level, so on any of them Back is blocked and you stay where you are. Back only closes sub-pages, innermost first:

| Sub-page | Back returns to |
| --- | --- |
| Event details (from any page) | The page underneath |
| A community in the forum (also from an event's "Related communities" link or a `#forum?community=…` URL) | All forum posts |
| A forum post or the Create post editor | The post list (or the open community) |
| Synthetic-data review (Settings → Team tools) | Settings |

How it works: switching tabs replaces the browser history entry instead of adding one, and each open sub-page owns one entry (`frontend/src/navigation.ts`). Each entry records its position, so the browser's Forward button is ignored instead of being mistaken for Back. The logo link no longer adds a history entry on each click. In-page Close / "Back to posts" buttons use up that entry, so a later Back doesn't land on a stale one. The old `hashchange` listener is gone; links and typed `#page` URLs are handled in the same `popstate` listener.

## Update — November 4, 2026: optional IBM watsonx interpreter

The AI Planner can now use IBM watsonx.ai (Granite, Dallas `us-south`) to understand chat messages. It is **off by default**: without configuration the app runs the simulated planner exactly as before, and no credentials are needed.

| Change | What teammates should expect |
| --- | --- |
| Live interpreter option | Starting Rust with `PLANNER_PROVIDER=watsonx` makes `/api/plan` send the student's message and the previous filters to watsonx.ai. The model returns only search filters (topics, days, times, food, cost, number of options). The schedule, profile, names and chat history are not sent. |
| Trusted matching unchanged | Model output must be a JSON object with only known fields and must pass `Constraints::validate`. Rust's deterministic planner still picks every event, so the model cannot invent event IDs, eligibility or food. Adding an event still needs the student's click and a fresh validation. |
| Honest labels | The chat status shows **Rust planner · IBM watsonx** only when watsonx actually answered. If watsonx times out (6 s), rejects authentication, errors or returns invalid output, that request uses the simulated planner, the label reads **Rust planner · Simulated**, and the reply starts with "IBM watsonx was unavailable…". The offline browser fallback is unchanged. |
| Secrets stay on the server | The API key is read from the server environment, is exchanged for an IBM IAM token server-side, and never appears in API responses, logs or browser code. `.env` files are git-ignored. |
| Health endpoint | `GET /api/health` now also reports `watsonx_configured`. `watsonx_connected` is true only after the most recent live call succeeded. |

### Run with watsonx

```sh
cp .env.example .env    # then fill in WATSONX_API_KEY and WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
set -a; source .env; set +a
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```

The startup line says which planner is active. `WATSONX_URL` defaults to `https://us-south.ml.cloud.ibm.com` and `WATSONX_MODEL_ID` to `ibm/granite-4-h-small`, the Granite chat model offered in the lab's watsonx Challenge Sandbox. If your project lists a different Granite chat model, set its ID instead. Leave `PLANNER_PROVIDER` unset (or `simulated`) for the credential-free classroom demo. - `backend/src/watsonx.rs`: `WatsonxInterpreter` (IAM token caching, `POST /ml/v1/text/chat`, JSON-only parsing, validation, timeout) and its mock-server tests.

## Architecture update — October 18, 2026

Enrollment, planning conversations and request interpretation now own their rules in separate modules. This keeps the calendar beside chat and mandatory demo RSVP flow while making asynchronous behavior testable through the same interfaces the UI uses.

| Change | What teammates should expect |
| --- | --- |
| Enrollment ownership | One module owns RSVP gating, pending additions, current-schedule checks and calendar/RSVP updates. Reset discards obsolete confirmations and errors; removing an event clears its RSVP. |
| Conversation ownership | Chat and replacement share request validity and busy-state handling. New chat/reset discard old results; changed schedules reject outdated suggestions. Replacement preserves every filter until the student explicitly changes it. |
| Consistent interpretation | “Professional”, “ceramics”, “balance”, “snack” and “refreshment” reach the interpreter. Rust and browser simulation distinguish unsupported requests from understood requests with no matches, and reject invalid clock input such as “before 11:99 am”. |
| Calendar beside chat | The **My calendar** button at the top right of AI Planner toggles a calendar panel on the right without leaving the conversation. It replaces the draft sidebar while open. On narrow screens it stacks below chat. |
| Actions in AI responses | New recommendation messages contain event cards with **View details** and **Add to calendar** buttons. Added events show a disabled confirmation button. Unavailable events show the reason. |
| Mandatory RSVP | Adding an event marked **RSVP required** opens a registration dialog. A demo attendee name and an explicit attendance checkbox are required before **Complete RSVP & add** can succeed. Cancelling or pressing Escape leaves the calendar unchanged. |
| Automatic calendar updates | A successful addition immediately updates the planner panel, dashboard and main calendar. Drop-in events can be added directly. Removing an event also clears its demo RSVP confirmation. |
| Shared enrollment validation | Every Add entry point—chat, draft plan, dashboard, Explore Events and event details—uses the same flow. Rust and the offline TypeScript fallback both enforce RSVP and current availability. |

The registration dialog is a **demo RSVP page** inside the app. It does not contact an organizer, reserve a real seat, charge a fee, or send a confirmation email. Use a fictional display name. There is no external registration website or live calendar integration.

### Implementation notes for the team

- `frontend/src/PlannerPanels.tsx` contains the chat event cards, side calendar, and RSVP form.
- `frontend/src/enrollment.ts` owns approved additions and removal, including latest-schedule validation and reset invalidation. `frontend/src/conversation.ts` owns chat and replacement lifecycle; suggestions never add events automatically.
- `frontend/src/App.tsx` renders views and handles navigation, notifications and dialogs. It subscribes to shared demo state and read-only workflow status through `useSyncExternalStore`.
- `frontend/src/interpretation.ts` owns browser request recognition, parsing and constraint validation. The Rust interpreter returns constraints plus recognition status; `POST /api/plan` now includes `understood`. Rebuild frontend and backend together.
- `frontend/src/api.ts` sends enrollment requests and supplies the explicitly labelled offline simulation. Backend request rejections are never treated as offline success.
- `backend/src/lib.rs` exposes `POST /api/enroll`. The Rust event model reads each record’s RSVP requirement from `data/events.json`; the client cannot override it.
- Browser-local state now records confirmed demo RSVP event IDs and event IDs attached to new chat responses. Existing saved schedules are preserved. Old chat messages remain readable but do not gain buttons retroactively; send a fresh prompt to see the new cards.
- `tests/workflows.test.ts` exercises complete enrollment and conversation outcomes with controlled request completion. Domain terms are documented in `docs/GLOSSARY.md`.

## Current boundaries

By default this version uses a Rust deterministic parser and template responses, with a labelled TypeScript fallback when the backend is unavailable. An optional watsonx.ai interpreter can replace the parser for understanding requests (see the latest update), but replies are still templates and events are still chosen by deterministic rules; it is not a general-purpose chatbot. Ambiguous natural language and unsupported constraints may not be understood; use the example prompts for the demo. “Start over” clears prior chat filters. It does not create real RSVPs, send messages, or sync calendars. Local discussion posts are not shared. Data is fixed, not live or fetched daily. The institution and business outcomes in the proposal remain hypotheses.

IBM Bob is a development assistant. This implementation was created in Codex and is not evidence of IBM Bob use. No React, no DOM. |
| [`tests/calendar-view.test.ts`](tests/calendar-view.test.ts) | **New.** 21 unit tests for all calendarGrid helpers. |
| [`frontend/src/CalendarView.tsx`](frontend/src/CalendarView.tsx) | **New.** Google-Calendar-style component with Day/Week/Month/Year views, toolbar (Today + ‹/› + title + switcher + Edit availability + Export), time grid (8 AM–9 PM), overlapping columns, "now" line, month chips, year mini-grids, demo-week banner. |

| [`frontend/src/styles.css`](frontend/src/styles.css) | Append all `.gcal-*` classes (toolbar, switcher, time-grid, event blocks, month/year grids, responsive breakpoints). No existing rules changed. |
| [`README.md`](README.md) | Add "Update — November 12, 2026" section with what changed, how to try it, test results, and known limits. |

### Commit

```
7090dc1  feat: Google-Calendar-style Day/Week/Month/Year views on My Calendar page
```

| Suite | Pass | Fail |
|---|---|---|
| `npm test` (TypeScript) | **112** | 0 |
| `npm run build` (tsc + Vite) | ✅ clean | — |
| `cargo test --locked` | **18** | 0 |

### Anything not finished or changed

- **No requirements were dropped.** All 10 numbered requirements are implemented.
- **Minor design choice:** The "+N more" chip in Month view acts as a "click to open Day view" (same as clicking the day cell), rather than opening a popover of overflowing events — this is the simplest correct behaviour and matches "Clicking a day opens Day view" from requirement 5.

- **Month/Year view classes:** Busy-class blocks are intentionally absent (requirement 7: "Do not show classes in Month or Year view").

## Bugs (must fix)

1. **Month view columns are uneven and misaligned.** Columns grow with their content (Tue and Thu are wide because of event chips), so day numbers no longer sit under the MON–SUN header (e.g. Oct 30, a Friday, appears almost under SAT).
   Fix: header and grid both use `grid-template-columns: repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr))`; chips are single-line with `text-overflow: ellipsis` and `overflow: hidden`; every column is the same width whatever the content.

2. **Week view header and grid are misaligned on phones.** At 375 px the time-grid columns are wider than the header columns and scroll sideways on their own, so Thursday's "Learning Sciences" shows under SAT. On desktop the inner vertical scrollbar also shifts the body ~1–9 px left of the header (Sunday is 9 px off).
   Fix: the header and the columns must always share the same column widths and scroll together horizontally (for example, put the header row inside the same horizontal scroll container as the grid and make it `position: sticky; top: 0`), and reserve the scrollbar space so desktop columns line up exactly (for example `scrollbar-gutter: stable` on both, or one shared scroll container).

3. **Year view: "today" is invisible.** Nov 2 has class `gcal-mini-cell gcal-mini-today gcal-mini-demo`; its text is white (rgb 255,255,255) on the pale demo-week green (rgb 241,249,242), so the "2" can't be seen.
   Fix: the today style must win over the demo-week style (dark green filled circle, white number), in Year view and in Month view.

4. **"Find an event" buttons are hidden.** They are positioned at `top: 100%` of each column, below the 9 PM line, so you only see them after scrolling the inner calendar to the very bottom.
   Fix: put a small "+" button in each demo-week weekday's column header (Week view) and next to the date in the Day view header, always visible without scrolling. Keep the accessible name "Find an event on Monday" etc. and the existing `onDay(i)` behavior. Remove the old bottom buttons.

5. **Month chips are not in time order.** Tue Nov 3 lists "3 PM Learning with AI" above "1 PM Designing your career story".
   Fix: sort chips by start time. Put the sorting in a pure helper in calendarGrid.ts and add a unit test for it.

## Polish (must fix)

6. **Chosen events look almost the same as classes** (pale green vs pale grey). Make chosen events clearly stand out using existing green tokens from styles.css (for example a stronger green fill or a solid green left border, like Google Calendar), and keep classes grey. Cancelled events keep their cancelled style.

7. **Event titles get cut off after one line** ("Designing your c…", "Learning with AI:…"). Let the title wrap to up to 2 lines when the block is tall enough (1-hour blocks and longer), then ellipsis. Add a `title` attribute with the full title and time so it shows on hover.

8. **The toolbar jumps when switching views.** In Day view the longer title ("Tuesday, Nov 3, 2026") pushes the Day/Week/Month/Year switcher onto a second line, so the buttons move under the mouse. At widths ≥ 1024 px keep the toolbar on one line in every view (for example give the title a fixed min-width, or put Edit availability / Export calendar on their own row so the switcher never moves). On phones wrapping is fine.

9. **"Demo week" is printed in all five demo-week cells in Month view.** Show the label once (on the Monday cell, or as one label spanning the row), keep the green background on all five days.

## Code cleanup

10. In `goToToday`, `setAnchor(today)` is called twice; remove the dead branch. In MonthView, `isDemoWeekRange && isInDemo` is redundant; use one check.

## Verify before committing
- npm test, npm run build, cargo test --locked: all must pass; report the counts.
- After `npm run build`, hard-refresh http://127.0.0.1:4173/#calendar and check, with at least 3 chosen events added from Explore Events:
  - Week and Month: day numbers/columns line up exactly under the header, at desktop width AND at 375 px width.
  - Year: Nov 2 is readable as today.
  - "+" Find an event is visible in the Week header for Mon–Fri of the demo week only.
  - Month chips are in time order; "Demo week" appears once.
  - Switching Day/Week/Month/Year at desktop width does not move the switcher.
- The Dashboard "week at a glance" strip must still look exactly as before.

## Commit
- Make NEW commit(s) on `Tingting` (do not amend 7090dc1), with clear messages, e.g. "Calendar: fix month/week column alignment, today in year view, visible Find an event".
- Update the README section "Update — November 12, 2026: Calendar Day/Week/Month/Year views" to mention these fixes and the new test count. Keep stating truthfully that the work was done with IBM Bob.
- Stage only the files you changed. Do NOT push.

1. What you changed for each numbered item (1–10), one line each.
2. Commit hashes and messages.
3. Test counts.
4. Any requirement you did not finish or changed, and why.

# Campus Compass

A runnable demonstration for the IBM AI Experiential Learning Lab, based on the supplied Campus Compass proposal and dashboard/planner prototypes.

## Start here (teammates)

**New to coding? Use the [project Wiki](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki).** It has copy-and-paste, step-by-step guides:

| Wiki page | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| [Getting started](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/Getting-Started) | Install the tools, download the project and run the website on your own computer. No IBM key needed. |
| [Using watsonx](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/Using-watsonx) | Optionally connect the AI Planner to IBM watsonx (Granite) with your own API key. |
| [IBM Bob](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/IBM-Bob) | Set up Bob IDE and export your Bob sessions, which the lab requires from every teammate. |
| [Team workflow](https://github.com/judyzhou666/ibm-campus_compass/wiki/Team-Workflow) | Update your branch, save your work and open a pull request. |

Quick start, once Node.js 22.12+ and Rust are installed:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:4173. The chat label under AI Planner shows which planner answered: **Rust planner · Simulated** (built-in rules, the default), **Rust planner · IBM watsonx** (live Granite), or **Browser fallback · Simulated** (the server is not running).

## Update — November 12, 2026: Calendar Day/Week/Month/Year views

**What changed:** The My Calendar page now has a Google-Calendar-style calendar with Day, Week, Month, and Year views, replacing the fixed Mon–Fri cards-only layout.

- **New files:**
  - `frontend/src/CalendarView.tsx` — Day/Week/Month/Year views with time grids, overlapping-event columns, "now" line, and navigation toolbar.
  - `frontend/src/calendarGrid.ts` — Pure date-math helpers (week/month/year grids, overlap layout, item position). No React, no DOM.
  - `tests/calendar-view.test.ts` — 21 unit tests for the date-math helpers.
- **Changed files:**
  - `frontend/src/App.tsx` — Calendar page now renders `<CalendarView>` instead of the `week(true)` strip. Dashboard strip and AI Planner panel are **unchanged**.
  - `frontend/src/styles.css` — New `.gcal-*` CSS classes appended at the end.

**How to try it:**
```sh
npm run build
cargo run --locked
```
Open http://127.0.0.1:4173/#calendar. Use the Day | Week | Month | Year switcher, the ‹ › and Today buttons, and click any event to open its details. Clicking a day in Month/Year view opens Day view for that date.

**Test results:**
- `npm test`: 112 TypeScript tests pass (up from 91), 5 Wiki tests pass.
- `npm run build`: clean TypeScript + Vite build, no new warnings.
- `cargo test --locked`: 18 Rust tests pass.

**Known limits / not implemented:**
- The "now" line is drawn at demo-clock time (Mon Nov 2, 9:00 AM), not the real wall clock, consistent with the rest of the app.
- No live-scroll to the current hour on open (grid can be scrolled manually).
- Month/Year views do not show busy-class blocks (by design per requirements — classes are weekly repeating in Day/Week only).
- The "+N more" chip in Month view opens Day view for that date (clicking any day cell does the same); individual event detail from Month chips is not added.
- This change was made with [IBM Bob](https://www.ibm.com/products/bob).

## Back and swipe-back between tabs — November 10, 2026

Back (and the swipe-back gesture) no longer steps through tabs you visited before. Sidebar tabs (Dashboard, My Calendar, Explore Events, Discussion Forum, AI Planner, Saved Events, Profile, Settings) are on the same level, so on any of them Back is blocked and you stay where you are. Back only closes sub-pages, innermost first:

| Sub-page | Back returns to |
| --- | --- |
| Event details (from any page) | The page underneath |
| A community in the forum (also from an event's "Related communities" link or a `#forum?community=…` URL) | All forum posts |
| A forum post or the Create post editor | The post list (or the open community) |
| Synthetic-data review (Settings → Team tools) | Settings |

How it works: switching tabs replaces the browser history entry instead of adding one, and each open sub-page owns one entry (`frontend/src/navigation.ts`). Each entry records its position, so the browser's Forward button is ignored instead of being mistaken for Back. The logo link no longer adds a history entry on each click. In-page Close / "Back to posts" buttons use up that entry, so a later Back doesn't land on a stale one. The old `hashchange` listener is gone; links and typed `#page` URLs are handled in the same `popstate` listener.

Verification: `npm test` (91 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build` and `npm run test:api` pass. In a fresh browser tab I pressed Back on every sidebar tab (all stayed put, three Backs in a row on Settings too), and checked event details (Back and Close button), the event → community link, community → post → Back → Back, switching communities, Create post with Back / "Back to posts" / Save Draft, the logo link, the search box, a typed `#calendar`, reloading on `#forum?community=ai`, and the data review returning to Settings. After review, a scripted run of 31 checks also covers Forward (community → post → Back → Forward changes nothing) and reloading partway through a session. Limitation: checked with `history.back()` in Chromium; the real iOS/macOS swipe gesture triggers the same browser Back but was not tried on a device.

## PR #9 review fixes — November 10, 2026

Fixes from the code review of the presentation-polish pull request, one commit each:

- **Undo** after adding an event now also puts it back in the planner's draft ideas, in its original position.
- **"Why this fits"** on planner results uses the topics the student asked for in chat, so it agrees with the folded evidence. Evidence times also convert "24:00" to "12:00 AM".
- **Toast:** the browser-storage warning no longer shows the previous toast's buttons. After pressing View calendar or Undo, keyboard focus moves to the page heading. Screen readers announce only the message, not the buttons.
- **Today marker** follows the chosen time zone. In Auckland or Sydney the demo clock falls on Tuesday, and the week strip now marks Tuesday to match the heading. The Settings note says what the time zone changes.
- **Styles:** the amber notice colors are defined once as `--notice-bg` and `--notice-ink`.

Verification: `npm test` (91 TypeScript tests, including 3 new ones in `tests/planner-display.test.ts`, and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build`, `cargo fmt --check`, Clippy with `-D warnings`, 18 Rust tests, `cargo build --locked` and `npm run test:api` all pass. In the built app I checked RSVP → add → Undo restoring the draft, View calendar moving focus to the calendar heading, the live region holding only the message, and the Auckland heading and today marker both showing Tue Nov 3.

## Presentation polish — November 10, 2026

A design critique of the prototype (saved in `.impeccable/critique/`, not committed) found problems that show during a live demo. Fixed, one commit each:

- **Dates agree.** The page heading used the real date (Nov 10) while the week strip showed Nov 2–6 with Monday marked today. The heading now shows the demo clock, **Mon, Nov 2, 9:00 AM · Demo week**, in the chosen time zone. The "today" marker on the week strip is a pill wide enough for "Nov 2".
- **Planner answers read as plain language.** Each result starts with "Why this fits: …" (interest, schedule, cost). The full planner evidence is folded under "How the planner checked this", with readable labels and 12-hour times. "Name coming soon" is gone from the status line; the honest **Rust planner / Browser fallback · Simulated** label stays.
- **Adding to the calendar ends well.** The confirmation toast offers **View calendar** and **Undo**. It stays up for 9 seconds and stays open while you hover over it or focus it.
- **Blocked events say so up front.** Event cards that conflict, are full, cancelled or need membership show the reason in amber and a **Can't add · See why** button that opens the details, instead of an "Add to calendar" button that fails.
- **Forum posts match the catalog.** Seed posts now name the right days for the Learning with AI lab, community dinner, sketchbook walk and resume peer review.
- **Copy:** "Welcome, Judy." on a first visit (then "Welcome back"), and "1 event" instead of "1 events".

**Demo tip:** to show the first-visit flow again, clear this site's storage in the browser (or run `localStorage.clear()` in the console) and reload.

Verification: `npm test` (88 TypeScript tests and 5 Wiki tests), `npm run build`, `cargo fmt --check`, Clippy with `-D warnings`, 18 Rust tests, `cargo build --locked` and `npm run test:api` all pass. In the built app I checked the heading date and today pill, a planner reply with the folded evidence, Add → Undo from the toast, the ten blocked cards on Explore, the forum post days and the first-visit greeting. Limitations: accessibility and mobile items from the critique (small text, tap targets, screen-reader structure) are deferred because this is a presentation prototype; the Rust planner's evidence text itself is unchanged, only how it is shown.

## PR #8 review fixes — November 5, 2026

## Update — November 4, 2026: optional IBM watsonx interpreter

The AI Planner can now use IBM watsonx.ai (Granite, Dallas `us-south`) to understand chat messages. It is **off by default**: without configuration the app runs the simulated planner exactly as before, and no credentials are needed.

| Change | What teammates should expect |
| --- | --- |
| Live interpreter option | Starting Rust with `PLANNER_PROVIDER=watsonx` makes `/api/plan` send the student's message and the previous filters to watsonx.ai. | Honest labels | The chat status shows **Rust planner · IBM watsonx** only when watsonx actually answered. If watsonx times out (6 s), rejects authentication, errors or returns invalid output, that request uses the simulated planner, the label reads **Rust planner · Simulated**, and the reply starts with "IBM watsonx was unavailable…". The offline browser fallback is unchanged. |
| Secrets stay on the server | The API key is read from the server environment, is exchanged for an IBM IAM token server-side, and never appears in API responses, logs or browser code. `.env` files are git-ignored. |
| Health endpoint | `GET /api/health` now also reports `watsonx_configured`. `watsonx_connected` is true only after the most recent live call succeeded. |
